elements.element: Vendor has a duty to defend covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 states that Vendor “shall defend” against the covered claims.

elements.element: Vendor has a duty to indemnify against covered claims and resulting losses, costs, expenses and reasonable attorneys' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 requires Vendor to indemnify against the claims and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees.

elements.element: Customer and its Affiliates are protected by Vendor's defence and indemnity.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 expressly identifies “Customer and its Affiliates” as the protected parties.

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity applies to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Covered claims include allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) covers allegations that the Services or Deliverables “infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Covered claims include claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(b) covers claims arising out of “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Covered claims include claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, which operatively implements the Vendor-caused data-breach trigger.

elements.element: Covered claims include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence.

elements.element: Covered claims include claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(d) expressly covers Vendor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires the indemnified party to give prompt written notice.

elements.element: The indemnifying party controls the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 gives the indemnifying party control of the defence.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 expressly requires reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity, if any, is limited to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 limits Customer's indemnity obligations to “third-party claims.”

elements.element: Customer-provided content is a permitted Customer-indemnity trigger.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(a) identifies content or materials provided by Customer as a permitted trigger.

elements.element: Customer's breach of law is a permitted Customer-indemnity trigger.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(b) identifies Customer's breach of Applicable Law as a permitted trigger.

elements.element: No Customer-indemnity grounds beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law are permitted.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 says Customer's obligations are “limited to” the two enumerated categories and states no additional grounds.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) provides Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual-property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims caused by combinations with other products, services or materials.
elements.evidence: No combinations exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims resulting from compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor may or must procure the right for Customer to continue using an infringing item.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no procure-right remedy.

elements.element: Vendor may or must modify an infringing item to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: Vendor may or must replace an infringing item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a refund if the other IP remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's IP-indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the operative language; the non-operative margin comment does not create one.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred Vendor defence and indemnity triggers, protected parties, procedure and limitation on Customer indemnity. It includes only terms needed to implement that preferred position and leaves the original warranty-disclaimer language intact. The fallback is not satisfied because, although the core Vendor IP indemnity is present, none of the customary exclusions, specified IP remedies or 3× annual-fees super-cap is operative. Drafting quality is materially reduced because Section 20.2 purports to limit “Customer's indemnity obligations” without actually creating any such obligations, despite the stated context that the Agreement previously contained no indemnity.
